statement: By multiplying $\\sum_{k=1}^{n}\\sin(k\\theta)$ by $2\\sin(\\theta/2)$ and using $2\\sin A\\sin B=\\cos(A-B)-\\cos(A+B)$, obtain a closed form for the sum.
solution: We have $2\\sin(\theta/2)\sum_{k=1}^{n}\\sin(k\\theta)=\\sum_{k=1}^{n}2\\sin(k\\theta)\\sin(\theta/2)=\\sum_{k=1}^{n}\bigl[\\cos((k-\\tfrac12)\\theta)-\\cos((k+\\tfrac12)\\theta)\bigr]$, which telescopes to $\\cos(\\theta/2)-\\cos((n+\\tfrac12)\\theta)$. Using $\\cos u-\\cos v=-2\\sin\\tfrac{u+v}{2}\\sin\\tfrac{u-v}{2}$, this equals $2\\sin\\tfrac{(n+1)\\theta}{2}\\sin\\tfrac{n\\theta}{2}$. Hence $\\sum_{k=1}^{n}\\sin(k\\theta)=\\dfrac{\\sin\\tfrac{n\\theta}{2}\\sin\\tfrac{(n+1)\\theta}{2}}{\\sin\\tfrac{\\theta}{2}}$ (for $\\sin(\theta/2)\\neq0$).
hints: Apply the product-to-sum identity to each term.
Convert the remaining difference of cosines back to sines.
